label: CONFIRMED: a hand-cleared goal returns through the no-entry fallback. The clear makes the resolving session carry nothing (relaunch-core goalLogEntry -> not active -> none) and removes goal_packet from the note; the next session has no goal entry, so latest is null with whole true and the fallback picks the first ancestor with budget ok and an unticked criterion, which is written to the note, consumed, and rendered as the /goal start prompt. The clear suppresses exactly one hop.

CONFIRMED: a met or failed goal whose goal.md still has an unticked line resurrects through the same no-entry path, because packetGoalIsSettable reads only the file and never the log. Today packet 039 and its parent have every criterion ticked and no higher ancestor holds goal.md, so the fallback currently carries nothing for this lineage; the path is live again as soon as a settable ancestor has an open criterion.

CONFIRMED: the tests cover the clearing hop but not the hop after it. The ended-goal test asserts a cleared goal yields empty inside the clearing session; the fallback test asserts an empty log yields the packet goal; no test feeds the fallback a session that immediately follows a clear. Smallest change: add that second call to the ended-goal test.

CONFIRMED: packetLineage is nearest-first and firstUsablePacket is a find, so a parent wins whenever every nearer goal is unsettable: absent child goal.md, all child criteria ticked, over-budget child slice, or a leaf phase child whose budget is unknown. Children 002 and 003 are Level 2 leaf phase children, so their own goals can never be carried and their phase parent always wins. The walk keeps going past that parent, so any older ancestor with an open criterion is equally eligible.

CONFIRMED: the no-entry fallback has no relation proof. The active-goal path requires the packet goal.md to carry the goal headline; the fallback checks only budget and an unticked box, so a stale ancestor with an open criterion is eligible even when the session works elsewhere (limitation 2 of child 002).

CONFIRMED: the smallest stale-parent fix is a relation bound. Option (a): pass lineage.slice(0, 2) at the fallback call, keeping the leaf-to-phase-parent case and dropping older ancestors. Option (b): pass the note goal headline and require the packet goal.md to carry it, mirroring the active-goal check, at the cost of a paraphrase miss. (a) is the smaller change; (b) is the freshness proof.

CONFIRMED: carrying the goal ending closes the cleared-goal case (item 1) but not the stale-parent case (item 2), because a stale parent is a different packet whose goal may never have ended. The 002 decision table also limits the ending idea to the cleared-goal gap.

CONFIRMED: the ending carrier is a new handoff-note frontmatter field such as goal_ended or goal_ending, written by recordGoalPacket and read by consume, then passed to the receiver through an env var beside SESSION_RELAUNCH_GOAL_PACKET. The pending record key set stays untouched, so the change is D3-neutral (D3 forbids a module and a relaunch record key). Cost: bin/session-relaunch.cjs, lib/relaunch-core.cjs, .skilled/bin/skilled-loop, plus resolver, CLI and wrapper tests.

CONFIRMED: the title-ending loss is real at the strip. The hop adds the receiver number at the launch argument; name_stem strips a trailing (sender_number) when sender_number >= 2, and the hop calls it with the post-increment count. A title ending in exactly the sender number is indistinguishable from a wrapper-written number and loses it; a test shows another number, Phase (7), survives. The frequency is UNCONFIRMED; the 003 limitation's example matches the code exactly.

CONFIRMED: the smallest title fix is to strip only a name the wrapper can prove it numbered. name_stem already receives the wrapper stem in SKILLED_LOOP_NAME; requiring a non-empty stem and an exact match of stem plus (sender_number) preserves a generated title in a never-named session (the 003 case) while keeping the intended strip for launched or renamed sessions. It is a wrapper change, not a record key.

CONFIRMED: the added ai-title search is one more tail read per Claude prepare. Each read starts at 262144 bytes and widens x4 to 16 MiB, re-reading from the end. ESTIMATE from constants, not measured: 0.25 MiB for a hit in the last 256 KiB; 21.25 MiB in four passes for a miss on a 16 MiB log. In readClaudeSettings it is the third search and the second title search, not the second search overall.

CONFIRMED: the goal search is the larger cost because the fallback requires a whole read to prove no goal entry: 21.25 MiB in four passes for a 16 MiB log, 3.25 MiB in three for a 2 MiB log (ESTIMATE from constants). Per Claude prepare the log is read by up to four tail searches, and the ai-title addition is one of the four, not the largest.

CONFIRMED: both goal bugs are Claude-only. resolveGoalPacketResult routes Claude to claudeGoalPacketResult, the record runtimes to recordedGoalPacket or handoverGoalPacket, and Codex to a reason with no packet.
The no-entry fallback runs only when the whole Claude log was read and holds no goal entry; a log cut at the 16 MiB tail cap carries nothing.
Children 002 and 003 are Level 2 leaf phase children; their own goals have no budget and always give way to the phase parent, which is why packet 039's goal is the one a child session carries.
The clear entry is parsed as inactive with an empty condition, so an ending latch cannot name the cleared packet from that line; it needs a boolean or a separately resolved packet.
